items.stem: Explain why the angles in a triangle add up to 180°, using a line drawn through one vertex parallel to the opposite side.
items.answer: The two angles next to the vertex on the parallel line are alternate to the other two angles of the triangle, and the three angles at the vertex lie on a straight line, so they add up to 180°.

items.stem: Explain why opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal.
items.answer: Adjacent angles are co-interior between parallel sides so each pair adds to 180°; each opposite angle is 180° minus the same angle, so opposite angles are equal.

items.stem: Explain the difference between corresponding and alternate angles.
items.answer: Corresponding angles are in matching positions at each intersection (an F shape); alternate angles are on opposite sides of the transversal between the parallel lines (a Z shape). Both pairs are equal.

items.stem: A, B and C lie on a circle with centre O, with C on the major arc. Angle AOB = 98°. Mohammed says angle ACB = 196° because "the angle at the circumference is double". Explain the mistake and find angle ACB.
items.answer: It is the angle at the centre that is double the angle at the circumference. Angle ACB = 98 ÷ 2 = 49°.
items.markingKey: B1 centre angle is twice circumference angle; B1 49° [2]

items.stem: TA is a tangent to a circle at A, and AB is a chord. Angle TAB = 64°. C is a point on the circle in the alternate segment. Arjun says angle ACB = 26°. Explain which theorem should be used and find angle ACB.
items.answer: The alternate segment theorem: the angle between the tangent and the chord equals the angle in the alternate segment, so ACB = 64°.
items.markingKey: B1 names alternate segment theorem; B1 64° [2]

items.stem: A, B and C lie on a circle with centre O, with C on the major arc AB. Angle AOB = (4x − 14)° and angle ACB = (x + 21)°. Find x and angle AOB, stating the circle theorem you use.
items.markingKey: B1 angle at centre = 2 × angle at circumference; M1 4x − 14 = 2(x + 21); A1 x = 28; A1 98° [4]

items.stem: A and B lie on a circle with centre O. Angle AOB = 64°. Find angle OAB, giving reasons.
items.markingKey: B1 OA = OB (radii) so triangle OAB is isosceles; M1 (180 − 64) ÷ 2; A1 58° [3]

items.stem: A, B, C and D are points on a circle with centre O. TA is the tangent to the circle at A. Angle TAB = 61° and angle ABD = 51°, where D is on the opposite side of AB from T. (a) Find angle ADB, giving a reason. (b) Find angle ACB, where C is on the same arc as D, giving a reason. (c) Find angle AOB, giving a reason.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 61°; B1 alternate segment theorem [2] (b) B1 61° (angles in the same segment) [1] (c) B1 122° (angle at centre = 2 × angle at circumference) [1]

items.stem: Ravi tries to construct the perpendicular bisector of a line AB of length 11 cm by drawing arcs of radius 4.5 cm from A and B. Explain why this does not work.
items.answer: The radius must be more than half of AB (5.5 cm); arcs of radius 4.5 cm do not meet, so there are no intersection points to join.
items.markingKey: B1 radius must exceed ½AB = 5.5 cm; B1 arcs do not intersect [2]

items.stem: A gardener in Muscat wants to plant a tree that is equidistant from two straight fences that meet at a corner, and exactly 4 m from the corner. Describe the constructions needed to find the position.
items.answer: Bisect the angle between the fences with ruler and compasses, then draw an arc of radius 4 m (to scale) centred at the corner; the tree is where the arc cuts the bisector.
items.markingKey: B1 angle bisector; B1 arc/circle radius from corner; B1 intersection [3]

items.stem: A scale drawing of a park in Riyadh uses a scale of 1 : 50000. On the drawing, a path constructed between two gates is 4.2 cm long. Find the real length of the path in metres.

Chloe draws triangle ABC accurately, with AB = 10 cm, BC = 6 cm and AC = 8 cm. (a) Show that angle ACB is a right angle. (b) Find the radius of the circle through A, B and C. (c) The bisector of angle ACB is constructed. Write down the angle it makes with CA.
items.answer: (a) 6² + 8² = 100 = 10², so by the converse of Pythagoras the angle opposite AB is 90°. (b) 5 cm (c) 45°
